body:
Thanks for the issue! If you're reporting a bug, please be sure to include:
1. The version of ESLint you are using (run `eslint -v`)
2. What you did (the source code and ESLint configuration)
3. The actual ESLint output complete with numbers
4. What you expected to happen instead

Requesting a new rule? Please see [Proposing a New Rule](http://eslint.org/docs/developer-guide/contributing/new-rules) for instructions.

I looked around and I could not find an example of `switch` in the `allman` style, but since the `allman` style is all about putting braces separate from the control statement, it seems to me the current implementation is incorrect.
Reproducible in the online demo. I agree. In allman style all braces should be on separate lines.
Ahh! Thanks @lo1tuma Forgot that it's already been fixed. Closing in favor of #3903 which has already been fixed.
Sorry guys, but that code is wrong. Comparing with "1tbs" is wrong, because "stroustrop" then fails to do the right thing. My version is correct.
@aparajita So you are saying the fix for #3903 introduced a new bug? If so, can you please file a new issue and give an example what kind of code causes the new bug?
Sorry, I don't have time. My version works. I'm not going to spend more time fixing someone else's bugs.
@lo1tuma It's quite unfair for you to ask me to show you why a wrong fix was accepted when I made the correct fix already. Isn't it your responsibility to verify the fixes?

issue.title: brace-style stroustrup fails on switch statement

labels.name: accepted
labels.description: There is consensus among the team that this change meets the criteria for inclusion

labels.name: archived due to age
labels.description: This issue has been archived; please open a new issue for any further discussion

repository.name: eslint
repository.description: Find and fix problems in your JavaScript code.

issue.body:
With the latest master `brace-style` with stroustrup option will fail on the following code:

``` js
switch(foo) {
  case "bar": break;
}
```

error message returned by ESLint is:

```
1:1  error  Opening curly brace appears on the same line as controlling statement  brace-style
```

This is a result of #3904. @aparajita already provided a PR with a fix for this issue here: #4003 

P.S. I think error message is also incorrect and should point to the brace that is causing a problem

body: @aparajita I haven’t asked you why the fix for #3903 was accepted. My question was what kind of new bug this fix introduced. Anyway @ilyavolodin filed an issue for this #4004.
